dedupe_keys.name: elpv defective solar cell image benchmark

description: The ELPV benchmark published by ZAE Bayern and collaborating researchers contains 2,624 electroluminescence images of solar cells extracted from 44 photovoltaic modules. Each image is an 8-bit, 300-by-300-pixel grayscale sample, with normalised size and perspective and corrected lens distortion. Annotations provide defect probability and monocrystalline or polycrystalline module type. Coverage is a laboratory/module sample collection, not a geographic plant inventory; acquisition dates and representativeness of deployed fleets are not established in the inspected README. A Python package loads images and annotations. The images are available free for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, while accompanying code is Apache-2.0; commercial use requires contacting the provider. A limitation is that image-based defect labels do not directly supply degradation rates, outage probabilities or site-level energy losses. The benchmark can support calibration and validation of photovoltaic condition models used in infrastructure simulations, complementing generation modelling such as PyPSA (model-pypsa). The repository links the original 2018 benchmark paper and later classification/segmentation articles. No images were downloaded.
